issue_context.title: Configure prompt for a single run
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

The CLI has a persistent config setting called `prompt`, which a user can enable or disable with 
```bash
gh config set prompt (enabled|disabled)
```

It would be helpful to have an environment variable with this functionality which forces no prompt for a single run, for example `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` or `GH_PROMPT=enabled` (names are just suggestions 😄 ).

### Proposed solution

Having an environment variable would allow users:
- to set this value for a single run or context, such as during the execution of a shell script or for a specific CLI command
- revert to the existing configuration when complete without having to store it before execution
- have the same semantics as other environment variables, such as `GH_HOST`

### Additional context

I think this can be achieved by adding a properly named environment variable and checking for it here: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/d21d388b8dc10c8f04187c3afa6e0b44f0977c65/pkg/cmd/factory/default.go#L178 before checking the config setting
comments: @mntlty This is a great idea, I am for adding it. I think the semantics of either `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` or `GH_NO_PROMPT=1` for the environment variable name make the most sense. I am opening this feature up for contributions 👍

review_comments: looking through the code this seemed like the only place to add to the tests, please let me know if I missed others!
